newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai Industrial buys cosmetics maker.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai Industrial buys cosmetics maker.

text.p: Shanghai Industrial Holdings Co Ltd has bought a troubled cosmetics maker in the city, Xia Fei Daily-use Chemical Factory, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

The Hong Kong-listed firm, the overseas investment arm of the Shanghai city government, spent 60 million yuan to acquire Xia Fei, which was once one of the top 10 cosmetics producers in China, the newspaper said.

Established in 1985, Xia Fei posted annual sales of 500 million yuan during its peak years but its annual turnover plunged to less than 100 million yuan last year due to fierce competition in China's cosmetics industry, the newspaper said.

Shanghai Industrial Holdings plans to merge Xia Fei with its existing cosmetics subsidiary, Shanghai Jahwa, and hopes to boost sales so that the combined operation controls over 10 percent of the domestic market in one or two years, it said.

It quoted Ge Wenyao, the firm's executive director, as saying the purchase was in line with the company's policy of using capital raised on overseas markets to "salvage teetering state enterprises and boost strong ones".
Shanghai Industrial Holdings was listed in Hong Kong in May last year.
